name: N2 ice at 46 K (an estimated index)
paper: the estimate's inputs: Peck and Khanna, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 56 (1966) 1059, from 468 nm; below, Bates, Planet. Space Sci. 32 (1984) 785, for N2's gas dispersion; A. F. Schuch and R. L. Mills, J. Chem. Phys. 52 (1970) 6000, DOI 10.1063/1.1672899, as the Crystallography Open Database gives it, entry 9012476, https://www.crystallography.net/cod/9012476.cif, SHA-256 c1bae956ec04070696962f7e2c4ecd1a2328f27b91081b92536ba74a72f1e96c, fetched 2026-10-14, for the cell
source: a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate, not a measurement (decision-r08-t5d rulings 3 and 5): the molar refraction of N2 from its gas dispersion as stated at 288.15 K and 101325 Pa (view/atmosphere/rayleigh.ts's row, Z = 0.999715), with no increment, since the solid is molecular, over the molar volume of hexagonal β-N2 (P6₃/mmc) at 46 K (28.25 cm³ mol⁻¹ from 93.810 Å³ and 2 molecules). The gas dispersion is measured over 254–2058.6 nm and extrapolated beyond. The measured visible n of N2 ice (Satorre et al. 2008, Planet. Space Sci. 56, 1748; Luna et al. 2012, Icarus 221, 186; at 632.8 nm, of films deposited cold) could not be read: closed. The method's checks on measured solids: Ar from its gas dispersion (Peck and Fisher, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 54 (1964) 1362) at the cell of E. R. Dobbs, B. F. Figgins, G. O. Jones, D. C. Piercey and D. P. Riley, Nature 178 (1956) 483, DOI 10.1038/178483a0, as the Crystallography Open Database gives it, entry 1541541, https://www.crystallography.net/cod/1541541.cif, SHA-256 4ac3ecee395a4f006797f4d74469aa7167deaa78a1c68c1b6c4c0bc17122fd23, fetched 2026-10-14 (a = 5.4 Å, four atoms) gives 1.2842 against Sinnock and Smith 1969's measured 1.2708 at 546.1 nm and 80 K (Phys. Rev. 181, 1297); NH3 ice 1.465 against Martonchik et al. 1984's 1.436 at 550 nm (Appl. Opt. 23, 541); and H2S ice at the density of an amorphous film at 19 K, 0.944 g cm⁻³, 1.439 against the 1.407 Yarnall and Hudson 2022 measure there at 670 nm (Astrophys. J. Lett. 931, L4; CC BY 4.0), each above the measurement. k = 0.
licence: estimated values from cited constants and a crystal cell from the Crystallography Open Database (its entry from the American Mineralogist Crystal Structure Database, usable with attribution to the journal article, which is given); no data set is copied (decision-r08-t5d ruling 5)
reduction: n = √((1 + 2x) ÷ (1 − x)), with x the gas's molar refraction over the solid's molar volume, evaluated on 380–780 nm every 5 nm to six significant figures; k = 0
standIn: a non-absorbing crystal whose real index is a Lorentz–Lorenz estimate from the gas's dispersion at the crystal's density, since no open visible optical constants of N2 ice were found: 1.256 at 380 nm, 1.250 at 550 nm and 1.248 at 780 nm
